title: Minimax Design and Estimation for Randomized Saturation Experiments with Bounded Clusters
banked_reason: Banked downgraded on 2026-09-09 during Lean formalization: the derivation had passed review at field tier, but the cold D0.5.G re-score under the projected-paper-score rule gave 7.4 and tier subfield, and the run was banked on that tier; the run did not fail and is a re-raise candidate.
tldr: Randomized saturation experiments reveal overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither a no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. Every realized interior cluster-label cell has a higher-order minimal nonface: with \(h\) equal to the larger treatment-arm size, all \(h\)-subsets of \(h+1\) same-arm coordinates are observable but the full set is not. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a label-constant menu, reduces exactly to a rational endpoint orbit game over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, and independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite complete positive-support saddle characterization: positive design orbits are dual best responses, positive prior orbits have primal risk equal to the value, and positive-likelihood cells use posterior means. The certified two-cluster instance has a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The bit-certified compiler returns weak rational certificates and a total zero-face-safe decoder without claiming rational exact optimizers.
gap: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators, while recent unrestricted minimax papers either assume no interference or replace observation feasibility by a pairwise conflict graph. None preserves the exact-count observation hypergraph while jointly optimizing the first-stage law and an arbitrary measurable estimator across the full feasible menu, including zero, full, and label-constant treated counts.
fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation; it then gives a general finite independent-design frontier, confines interiority to the higher-order obstruction, equality witness, and strict rational separation certificate, and confines saturation variation to the last two, while exposing bit complexity and zero-face decoding as the open task.
